page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable compute instance driven by the AWS Nitro System. Powered by Intel Xeon 8488C processors operating at a nominal clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU supports modern vector and acceleration instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, AMX INT8, and VNNI. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 running at 5 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local NVMe storage is not bundled with this configuration, and attached block storage must rely on external network-attached volumes. Networking baseline throughput is rated at 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded throughput alongside competent multi-core metrics. In Geekbench testing, the m7i-flex.8xlarge achieved a single-core score of 2,023.0 (top 25%) and a multi-core score of 15,569.0. It demonstrates strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.42 GB/sec as well as Geekbench image and text processing. Static web serving throughput reached 48.18 GB/sec, placing it within the upper quartile. Standard multi-core and memory evaluations—such as stress-ng multi-core (32,413.77), PassMark CPU (47,332.26), and Redis SET operations (39.29 million ops/sec)—fall into the mid-tier category. In CPU-based LLM inference, text generation throughput is strong on lightweight 135M models (332.68 tokens/sec) but degrades considerably to 2.67 tokens/sec on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators.

Architecturally, the Flex profile delivers general-purpose performance optimized for cost efficiency relative to fixed-baseline instances. Because the CPU allocation is burstable, workloads that maintain sustained maximum core utilization over extended periods may encounter throttling tradeoffs compared to full provisioned instances. Furthermore, the lack of local NVMe storage means disk-intensive pipelines depend heavily on network storage bandwidth.

The m7i-flex.8xlarge fits workloads characterized by variable CPU demand, including web serving, application backends, mid-sized relational database environments, caching layers, and software compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 burstable vCPUs across 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8488C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it incorporates 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and lacks dedicated GPU accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks show upper-quartile capability in single-core performance, text and image processing, gzip compression, and static web serving throughput (48.18 GB/sec), while sustained multi-threaded execution and PassMark metrics align with mid-range baselines. Due to its burstable allocation profile and cost-optimized design, the m7i-flex.8xlarge is suited for variable computing requirements such as dynamic web servers, intermediate build runners, caching servers, and general enterprise application hosting.
